camps.name: Eldorado-Inspiration Glacier saddle high camp
camps.why: The high camp for every route on this peak: rock-walled tent sites on the glacier apron near 7,500 ft, fully exposed, with the summit one pre-dawn push away. Carry water or melt snow.

camps.name: Roush Creek Basin
camps.why: Lower camp at 6,100-6,400 ft with running water, over the ridge from the boulder field. Suits a short first day or a late start, but you regain the height next morning.

camps.name: Eldorado Creek Basin
camps.why: First flat ground at about 5,500 ft, but the meadow is protected and camping here is discouraged. Use it only if the boulder field slows you badly.

plan_conflict: On file Roush Creek Basin is main and Eldorado Creek Basin is called the usual first camp; parties actually sleep both nights at the high camp, so both changed to route.

camps.name: Marble Creek Campground, Cascade River Road
camps.why: Car campground eight miles up the Cascade River Road. Handy the night before a dawn start or while permits are sorted, but it gains you no height.

camps.name: Eldorado East Ridge rock bivies
camps.why: Flat rock near the base of the East Ridge (7,500-7,800 ft) where the snow has melted back: firmer and drier than the glacier, used in place of the snow camp, not as an extra stop.

camps.name: Buckner cross-country zone bivy
camps.why: High bivy under Buckner's north side for parties who want to sleep on the route. Needs its own zone permit and a site a mile from any designated camp; not where most parties stay.

camps.name: Sahale Glacier Camp
camps.why: Rock-walled tent sites at the top of Sahale Arm; the usual base for Horseshoe. Permits are scarce, water means glacier melt, and the basin is a steep drop below.

camps.name: Pelton Basin Camp
camps.why: Permitted camp just below Cascade Pass on the Stehekin side. A fallback without a Sahale permit, but a longer walk to Horseshoe Basin and a long summit day.

camps.name: Basin Creek Camp
camps.why: Three-site valley camp near the Horseshoe Basin trail junction at about 3,200 ft. Closest designated camp to the cirque, but small and far from the pass approach.

camps.name: Doubtful Lake Camp
camps.why: Lakeside camp in a cirque below Sahale Arm with sure water. A middle stop that splits the approach, but not on the usual one-night trip to Sahale Glacier Camp.

plan_conflict: Buckner cross-country zone bivy was listed main alongside Sahale Glacier Camp; most parties sleep at Sahale Glacier Camp, so the bivy is now route.

camps.name: Kool-Aid Lake
camps.why: Small lake camp at about 6,120 ft just below Cache Col; the standard stop for Hurry-Up. Water on the spot and the peak is a short morning from camp.

plan_conflict: No camp is on file and no source found names the East Ridge nights; a recent report approached through the Jerry Lakes basin, but it was not confirmed as the camp, so nights 1 and 2 are left unassigned.

camps.name: High camp below the Nohokomeen Glacier
camps.why: Camp on the ridge below the glacier toe near 5,200 ft, three brushy miles past May Creek. Leaves a manageable summit day; some parties push on to a glacier camp near 7,800-8,000 ft.

camps.name: May Creek Camp, Ross Lake
camps.why: Designated camp eight easy miles in, at the foot of the bushwhack. A lower, easier base for parties who arrive late; one party slept here both nights and climbed from it.

plan_conflict: Sources differ: some parties camp at May Creek both nights and others use a 7,800-8,000 ft glacier camp; the plan's 5,200 ft camp is the middle choice.

camps.name: May Creek Camp, Ross Lake
camps.why: Designated camp eight easy miles up the East Bank Trail where the off-trail climb begins; the usual first night, reached by trail or water taxi.

plan_conflict: Night 2 (the plan's camp below the ridge) is not on file and no source confirmed it; one earlier North Ridge trip went up and over via the East Ridge and out the Crater Mountain side rather than back to the East Bank Trailhead.

camps.name: Camp on the east side of Jack
camps.why: The only camp for this route, near 6,000 ft on Jack's east side past the Jerry Glacier crossing; it is also the base for the summit day and the return over the pass.

plan_conflict: No trip report found for this route; the camp and nights come from the plan and the camp on file.

camps.name: Crater Creek Meadows bench
camps.why: Heather bench at about 6,000 ft above Crater Creek; the staging camp for the south face. Closer to the face than Jerry Lakes, but less scenic and farther from lake water.

camps.name: Jerry Lakes basin
camps.why: Grassy bowl with several sites by the lakes, snow-free by mid-August and easy if you arrive late. Reports show parties using it, but the traverse to the face is longer.

camps.name: Jerry Lakes Peak south saddle
camps.why: Exposed ledge, not a camp: on record only as an unplanned night out in a bivy sack. Know it exists if caught on the ridge, and plan not to use it.

plan_conflict: The plan's day 2 repositions camp toward the Jerry Lakes saddle, so night 2 may not be at the night 1 camp; Jerry Lakes basin demoted from main to route to keep one main per night.
No camp is on file; trip reports use Jerry Lakes basin for nearby routes but no elevation was confirmed, so no new camp was added and nights 1 and 2 are left unassigned.

camps.name: Little Jack camp, knoll northwest of Little Jack
camps.why: A 6,600 ft rise a short way northwest of Little Jack, about six hours in. Across Crater Creek from Jack, so summit day leaves from camp and the exit is one descent.
